title: Framed homotopy function complexes and derived pushouts of simplicial categories
statement:
Give the category $\mathrm{sCat}$ of small simplicial categories the Bergner model structure: its weak equivalences are the Dwyer--Kan equivalences, with generators and path-component categories as in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting] and [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-cell-stability]. Write $h\mathrm{sCat}$ for the localization at Dwyer--Kan equivalences, computed by cofibrant-fibrant replacements and cylinder homotopy classes. Universes contain all diagrams and ordinary Hom sets used below. Use the cosimplicial Reedy model structure and latching objects of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], and Kan complexes and homotopy pullbacks as in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For a cofibrant replacement $QA\to A$, a frame means an augmented cosimplicial object $A^\bullet\to\operatorname{const}(QA)$ with $A^0=QA$, each augmentation $A^n\to QA$ a weak equivalence, and every latching map $L_nA^\bullet\to A^n$ a cofibration, including $n=0$. Such frames exist and may be chosen functorially. For a fibrant replacement $T\to RT$ define the homotopy function complex by
$$\operatorname{Map}^h(A,T)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sCat}}(A^n,RT),$$
with simplicial operators given by precomposition with the cosimplicial operators. The Hom on the right is the ordinary set of enriched functors, with no simplicial model structure on $\mathrm{sCat}$ assumed. These complexes are Kan, are independent up to natural weak equivalence of the replacement and frame choices, and are homotopy invariant in both variables. There is a natural bijection $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}^h(A,T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(A,T)$, compatible with restriction and composition. A representative $QA\to RT$ induces a functor $\pi_0A\to\pi_0T$, up to natural isomorphism, by using the equivalences $\pi_0QA\to\pi_0A$ and $\pi_0T\to\pi_0RT$; this depends only on its homotopy class.

For any small span $A\leftarrow X\to B$, let $P$ be the ordinary pushout of a cofibrant replacement of the span (a span of cofibrant objects with both structure maps cofibrations). The restriction comparison is a natural weak equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}^h(P,T)\simeq\operatorname{Map}^h(A,T)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}^h(X,T)}\operatorname{Map}^h(B,T).$$
For any small family $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ the disjoint-union coproduct satisfies the natural restriction comparison
$$\operatorname{Map}^h(\coprod_{i\in I}A_i,T)\simeq\prod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Map}^h(A_i,T),$$
including the empty family. These comparisons commute with the cocone restrictions and maps of spans and families, so that maps of spans induce maps of their derived pushouts in $h\mathrm{sCat}$, compatible with identities and composition.
